newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end firm on late technical buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end firm on late technical buying.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on Friday after struggling most of the session as a late spurt of technical and commercial buying pulled the market out of the doldrums, traders said.

In the last minutes of trading, Iowa Grain reportedly bought two million bushels January while Cargill Inc and ADM each bought 500,000 bushels January which further fueled the late rally, traders said.
Soybeans had traded mixed most of the day amid rumors a major exporter was loading 400,000 tonnes of soybeans on the St. Lawrence river.
But traders downplayed the likelihood of the rumor, noting tight availability of soybeans due to an active export pace and strong soybean crushing rates.
Still, CBOT reported Friday afternoon that soybean registrations dropped by more than 1.5 million bushels, which added to ideas the soybeans were being shipped.
Grain registrations in Chicago were at 3.305 million bushels as of Friday, down 1.565 million bushels from the previous day, CBOT reported.
Soybeans closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher to one cent lower with January up 3-1/2 at $7.09-1/2.
On the day, commercials were mostly on the buy side and funds were said to be sellers, traders said.
ADM, Cargill Inc, Produce Grain and Term Commodities were all said to be buyers of soybeans on the day while Refco Inc, FIMAT Futures and Prudential Securities were sellers.
Traders pointed to technical trade, noting support held at $7.02 per bushel. Resistance was pegged at $7.11 per bushel which was also the session high.
